title: Integrating Sperm Microscopy and Lifestyle Factors for Male Fertility Analysis
author: Oguri, Tomoko
materials: Data on baseline characteristics were collected through these structured self-administered questionnaires and through physician-conducted interviews for clinically complex eligibility items. Demographic and socioeconomic factors included age, height, weight, educational attainment, marital status, and household income [46]. Regarding medical background, current and past medical histories were obtained. Regarding current medications, we verified the use of treatments for androgenetic alopecia, drugs for erectile dysfunction, and zinc supplementation. Furthermore, as part of the reproductive background, the partner’s pregnancy history, history of infertility treatment [47,48], the participants’ desire for children [49], and experience using home sperm-testing kits [50] were investigated.

Furthermore, the Aging Males’ Symptoms Scale (AMS) score [70-72] was used as an indicator of physical and psychological changes associated with androgen decline. The National Institutes of Health Chronic Prostatitis Symptom Index (NIH-CPSI) [73] was used to evaluate chronic prostatitis symptoms. These measures were included to support exploration of potential infertility risk factors and hypothesis generation.

steps.title: Obtain approvals and register study
steps.instruction: Register the study in the UMIN-CTR (registration number UMIN000060395; registration date January 18 2026; disclosure date January 19 2026) and obtain ethical approval from all participating institutions (e.g., Osaka Pharmacology Clinical Research Hospital IRB #R01114a, review December 18 2025, notification December 19 2025; AIST IRB #Life 2025‑0618, review January 6 2026, notification January 7 2026; plus approvals from Tsukuba, Gakuen, International University of Health and Welfare, Nagoya, and NIES).

steps.title: Define eligibility and enrollment targets
steps.instruction: Set group‑specific inclusion criteria: Group 1 – men 18‑24 y, ≥10 ejaculations/month, BMI 18.5‑<25 kg/m², never smoked; Group 2 – men 18‑41 y, ≥1 ejaculation/month, attend visits 8:00‑11:00 A.M., fast the night before, complete two visits. Apply exclusion criteria to both groups (congenital reproductive anomalies, varicocele, malignancy, endocrine disease, prior hormone therapy, cognitive impairment, acute illness). Record lifetime smoking <100 cigarettes, no smoking in past 6 months, none during study. Exclude participants using thyroid hormone preparations or 5α‑reductase inhibitors within past 6 months; allow minoxidil; generally permit corticosteroids except for autoimmune disease; allow topical/inhaled corticosteroids. Set enrollment targets: 25 participants for Group 1 and 100 participants for Group 2 (co‑enrollment allowed).

steps.title: Recruit participants and obtain consent
steps.instruction: Recruit men residing in Japan from the InCROM volunteer panel (not from infertility clinics) between January 18 and February 21 2026. After eligibility confirmation, schedule visits at Osaka Pharmacology Clinical Research Hospital, obtain written informed consent, and provide reimbursement (Group 1 JPY 10,000 total; Group 2 JPY 15,000 total – JPY 5,000 on explanation day and JPY 10,000 on study day).

steps.title: Collect baseline questionnaires and conduct interviews
steps.instruction: Administer paper‑based self‑administered questionnaires covering demographics, socioeconomic status, medical history, medication use, reproductive background, occupational exposures, lifestyle habits (smoking, alcohol, sauna/bathing), nutrition (BDHQ), sleep (PSQI‑J), chronotype (rMEQ), physical activity (IPAQ), psychological status (PSS, K6), sexual function (SHIM, modified SHIM, EHS, MSHQ‑EjD‑SF, ejaculation latency, desire scales), AMS, and NIH‑CPSI. Have study staff check completeness on site. Conduct physician‑led interviews using a prespecified checklist to confirm eligibility, clarify complex medical/reproductive history, and verify medication details. Allow “prefer not to answer” for sensitive items.

steps.title: Perform physical measurements (Group 2 only)
steps.instruction: Measure body composition with a TANITA MC‑780A (weight, BMI, body‑fat %, muscle mass, segmental muscle mass, skeletal muscle mass index, fat‑mass index, phase angle, extracellular‑water/total‑water ratio) while participants are barefoot and in light clothing; correct for clothing weight. Record grip strength twice for each hand using TAKEI 5401, adopt the maximum value. Record back‑muscle strength twice with TAKEI 54021 (upper body inclined 30°, knees extended, not locked), adopt the maximum value. Measure waist circumference at the midpoint between lower rib margin and iliac crest, and maximum hip, thigh, and calf circumferences with a SECA 201 non‑stretchable tape; repeat each measurement twice and perform a third if the two differ by ≥1 cm.

steps.title: Collect semen sample
steps.instruction: Verify a 48‑to‑<144 h ejaculatory abstinence period upon arrival. Have the participant masturbate in a designated room and immediately complete the “Subjective Assessment at Collection” questionnaire (record abstinence period, any spillage, time taken for collection, orgasm intensity on a 4‑point Likert scale, subjective semen volume compared to usual, subjective time compared to usual, and stress level on a 10‑point Likert scale). Liquefy the sample in a 37 °C incubator or at room temperature for up to 60 min; if a thread ≥2 cm remains during pipetting, mechanically agitate with an 18‑gauge needle. Determine semen volume by weighing the collection container and assuming a density of 1.0 g/mL.

steps.title: Conduct automated semen analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the liquefied sample using the LensHooke X3 PRO system (Bonraybio). Measure sperm concentration and total motility according to WHO 6th Edition criteria. Record detailed kinematic parameters: fast progressive, slow progressive, non‑progressive, immotile categories; average path velocity (VAP), straight‑line velocity (VSL), curvilinear velocity (VCL), amplitude of lateral head displacement (ALH), beat‑cross frequency (BCF), linearity (LIN), straightness (STR), wobble (WOB). Determine percentage of normal morphology, pH, and round‑cell concentration via the system’s automated image‑recognition. Measure static oxidation‑reduction potential with MiOXSYS (Caerus Biotech) to assess sperm oxidative stress. Save microscopic videos in native format with full metadata (frame rate, resolution).

steps.title: Process and store residual semen
steps.instruction: Prepare Diff‑Quik stained smears from residual semen for morphological evaluation using Kruger’s strict criteria. Aliquot the remaining semen (volume dependent on what is left after onsite testing) into cryovials, freeze at ‑80 °C, and ship to collaborating institutions or external laboratories. Frozen aliquots will later be used for SCSA‑derived DNA fragmentation index (DFI), high DNA stainability (HDS), trace and major element analysis, chemical speciation, and biomarker assays (inhibin B, INSL3).

steps.title: Collect blood and urine (Group 2 only)
steps.instruction: Instruct participants to fast (no breakfast) on the study day, finish dinner by ≈ 9:00 P.M. the night before, and allow water intake. Collect an early‑morning urine sample and a fasting blood sample between 8:00 and 11:00 A.M., before semen collection. Process blood into plasma or serum, aliquot, and freeze at ‑80 °C for later shipment.

steps.title: Perform urine assays
steps.instruction: Analyze urine for environmental chemicals (phthalate esters, parabens, pesticides), soy isoflavones, trace and major elements, element speciation, creatinine, specific gravity, and urea nitrogen.

steps.title: Perform blood assays
steps.instruction: Measure serum/plasma gonadotropins and sex‑steroid profile (FSH, LH, testosterone, free testosterone, DHEA‑S, SHBG, DHT, estradiol, prolactin, AMH, inhibin B, INSL3), metabolic markers (albumin, fasting glucose, insulin), and exposure substances (PFAS, trace and major elements, element speciation) in whole blood, serum, and plasma.

steps.title: De‑identify and ship samples
steps.instruction: Assign each participant a study identification code; keep the linkage key only at Osaka Pharmacology Clinical Research Hospital. Send coded semen, blood, and urine samples to collaborating laboratories or external facilities for the assays described above.

steps.title: Quality‑control DFI measurement (Group 1)
steps.instruction: Use Group 1 samples to assess intraday, interday, and inter‑facility variability of the SCSA‑based DFI and HDS assays. Adjust flow‑cytometry gating settings accordingly, establish reference ranges, and exclude outliers before proceeding to primary association analyses.

steps.title: Store data and conduct statistical analyses
steps.instruction: Enter all questionnaire responses, physical measurements, semen parameters, DFI values, and assay results into the centralized multimodal database. Summarize continuous variables as means ± SD or medians (IQR); categorical variables as frequencies (%). Treat DFI as a continuous outcome; also explore categorical thresholds (15 % and 27 %). Perform correlation and simple linear regression for continuous DFI, logistic regression for categorical DFI, and sensitivity analyses as described. Use two‑sided tests with α = 0.05; report effect sizes and 95 % CIs; apply log‑transformations or creatinine/sg corrections where appropriate.
